kills.property: A user who has deposited amount d can successfully withdraw exactly d; the withdrawal must not revert.
kills.change_summary: Replace the guard `require(amount <= balances[msg.sender])` with `require(amount < balances[msg.sender])` so a full-balance withdrawal reverts, leaving the balance unchanged.

kills.property: A fresh caller (no recorded deposit) can never successfully withdraw a positive amount: withdraw(amount) must revert unless amount is 0.
kills.change_summary: Replace the require(amount <= balances[msg.sender]) check with require(amount <= type(uint256).max) so any amount can be withdrawn regardless of balance.

kills.property: After a deposit of d and a withdrawal of a (a<=d), refund() must return exactly the remaining balance d-a to the caller; the mutant never decrements the balance, so refund() tries to pay d with only d-a in the contract and reverts, leaving the caller short.
kills.change_summary: Delete the statement `balances[msg.sender] -= amount;` so the caller's balance is never reduced after withdrawal.

kills.property: For any admissible deposit, migrateTo by the creator to a recipient that refuses ETH must revert (the transfer fails), so the call cannot silently succeed; the mutant pays the creator instead, succeeds, and empties the contract.
kills.change_summary: Send the contract's remaining balance to the creator instead of the given address.

kills.property: For any recipient distinct from the contract itself, once the contract holds funds, the creator calling migrateTo must move the entire balance out so address(c).balance == 0; the mutant transfers 0 and leaves the funds in place.
kills.change_summary: Transfer zero instead of the contract's balance, so migrateTo no longer moves any funds out of the contract.

kills.property: After depositing d and withdrawing a (2 <= a <= d), a caller must never be able to withdraw more than the remaining balance d-a even if the contract holds extra padding funds; the reference always reverts on the over-withdrawal while the mutant (which decremented the balance by only 1) lets it succeed for a >= 2.
kills.change_summary: Replace `balances[msg.sender] -= amount;` with `balances[msg.sender] -= 1;` so the balance decrement no longer matches the withdrawn amount.
